description.text: The set of channels to use as the displacement map source.

impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.
The size of the filter used when sampling the input image.
When enabled the mask in this node is injected into the node directly below it if that node has the default path mask set.

Patterns to match prim names to using standard glob-style wildcards '*', '?'. There can be multiple mask patterns separated by spaces.
  • Default - selects the default prim(s) for the node. The default will be the injected mask prim paths if there is an upstream node with this. Otherwise the default mask for this node type is evaluated.
  • All Roots - selects the top level Xform(s) in your scene graph
  • Last modified - selects whatever the last node modified
  • All Cameras - selects all Cameras in your scene graph
  • All lights - selects all Lights in your scene graph
  • All Meshes - selects all meshes in your scene graph
  • Custom - sets a custom selection of prims that exist in your scene graph
An offset added to X, Y, and Z when displacing vertices.

Recalculate normals based on input geometry topology. This can be useful if the input geometry has no normals or they are incorrect. The "Normals" node can also be used for this if more control is required.
An overall multiplier that scales the amount of displacement at each vertex.

How vertex positions are affected by the displacement image.
  • luminance, red, green, blue, alpha: offset each vertex along its normal by the given image channel value
  • rgb absolute: set each vertex's XYZ position to the values in the image channels
  • rgb relative: offset each vertex's current XYZ position by the pixel values, ignoring the current point's normal
The attribute to use as UV map. If empty, uses the first found from: primvars:st, primvars:uv, primvars:st_0, primvars:st_1, primvars:st0, primvars:st and st.
An additional factor that scales the X, Y, and Z displacements separately.

description.plain_text: GeoDisplace is a modifier that moves each vertex in the input geometry by the pixel value that corresponds with it in the input image. The geometry's UV map is used to sample the pixel value to use at each vertex.There are several ways you can displace the input geometry based on the image. The simplest is to use a single channel to drive a displacement along the vertices' normals. For this, choose luminance, red, green, or blue as the source. You can also use three channels. In this case, you can select rgb absolute to move the vertices to absolute positions defined by the pixel values if the channels are XYZ render pass, or select rgb relative to offset the existing vertex XYZ positions by the values of the three channels of image input.
description.text:
GeoDisplace is a modifier that moves each vertex in the input geometry by the pixel value that corresponds with it in the input image. The geometry's UV map is used to sample the pixel value to use at each vertex.

There are several ways you can displace the input geometry based on the image. The simplest is to use a single channel to drive a displacement along the vertices' normals. For this, choose luminance, red, green, or blue as the source. You can also use three channels. In this case, you can select rgb absolute to move the vertices to absolute positions defined by the pixel values if the channels are XYZ render pass, or select rgb relative to offset the existing vertex XYZ positions by the values of the three channels of image input.
